Environmental Ed Day 7 Overwhelmed

Oct 12, 2010 • Janice Cotcher

We did not have class today but I did start panicking about my Action Learning Project. I thought spending the weekend at my grandparents’ farm would be the perfect opportunity to learn about how to eat more locally. I was a little discouraged because it seemed like only the “old timers” are the ones who locally. My cousins and friends who are around my age buy most of their groceries. They are busy with work, family and children and there never seems to be enough time.

Am I taking on too much with trying a prairie diet? It feels like if you don’t have the money to buy more locally produced food (which is usually more expensive) you need the time, effort and land to produce your own. It all seems so overwhelming right now. I am so busy with school and I’m worried that I am doing too much for Action Learning Project. I think I need to rethink things…

Speaking of anxiety, I have to ride a bike on Wednesday for the first time in about 13 years. My class is taking a trip around Wascana Lake. I’m worried about

  • falling
  • traffic
  • falling in traffic
  • being too slow
  • being too out of shape (using muscles I have not used in a looooooong time) where I’m going to lock up my bike
  • how I’m going to get the bike to school (not all buses have bike racks and I have no idea how to use them)
  • I don’t remember how to change gears on a bike

I road my mom’s bike around the block and I was terrified of going too fast. This could be interesting. I am going camping next weekend for class and I am more anxious about this bike ride than camping. Let me re-frame this, I am more scared to ride a bike than to GO CAMPING IN SASKATCHEWAN IN THE MIDDLE OF OCTOBER WITH NO FACILITIES.
